text:
Alex R: Quick sync — chargeback implications if we route Tenant42 traffic into eu-west during failover? Need a short checklist for the RFC follow-up.

Jing Li: Good call. Main question: billing attribution. Do we charge tenant to their home region or to the region that actually served the request? That drives invoicing and finance signals.

Devon M: Today we tag by cluster_id at allocation time. When failover happens the cluster -> region mapping changes, so cost flows to the serving region. Finance will likely object if it flips.

Priya S: Legal/privacy angle: for residency-restricted tenants we must record where data was processed. Billing is a separate axis, but customers will expect alignment. We should decouple residency metadata from billing metadata.

Alex R: High-level options: A) Anchor billing to tenant.home_region (stable, predictable). B) Bill to compute.region (accurate for infra costs). C) Hybrid/recon with policies (e.g., warmup billed to served, steady-state to home). Tradeoffs: transparency vs reconciliation complexity.

Jing Li: Tech constraints — routing layer only surfaces final region id. To do (A) we need to propagate tenant.home_region through edge proxy -> sidecars -> logging/billing. Could add an `X-RD-Home-Region` header.

Devon M: We already have an internal debug header `X-RD-Region`, small delta to add home-region. Downstream billing pipeline needs to ingest it though.

Priya S: Also need explicit audit logs: record both home_region and served_region per request for compliance. That satisfies both billing and legal.

Alex R: Proposed minimal action items (for RFC follow-up):
1) Add `home_region` propagation in edge proxy (header defaulted from tenant record).
2) Persist `home_region` + `served_region` in request logs and traces.
3) Billing pipeline: add a reconciliation job to attribute costs per-tenant according to tenant.policy: `home` | `served` | `hybrid`.
4) Console: surface per-tenant cost attribution and mark events when served != home.
5) Tests: simulate failover + warmup to validate attribution rules.

Jing Li: Edge cases: cache/kv warmups where ephemeral compute runs in other region — hybrid rule suggestion: first N seconds (30s?) billed to served for cold-start costs, then revert to home. Thoughts? :thinking:

Devon M: Implementation note: headers can be spoofed if proxies are untrusted. We should HMAC-sign the routing headers: `X-RD-Region-Sig` = HMAC(K, tenant_id|home_region). Proxy signs; downstream validates. Key rotation via KMS.

Alex R: Agree on signing. Who owns key rotation? infra team. We'll call it out in the RFC.

Priya S: Compliance asks: retention window for these logs (and signatures) — legal prefers long retention for audits, but we should balance with storage. I'll confirm but add as a checklist item (retention + redaction rules).

Jing Li: Can someone size the work? My rough: proxy header + signing (2w), logging + billing pipeline + recon job (3w), Console + docs (1w) — staggered across teams.

Devon M: I'll take the proxy PR and put up a prototype: header add + sig hmac using our sidecar key. Will also add tests for spoofed header rejection.

Alex R: I'll draft the RFC follow-up section with the exact header spec and example. Quick example for the thread:
```
X-RD-Home-Region: eu-west-1
X-RD-Served-Region: us-east-1
X-RD-Region-Sig: v1:base64sig
```

Priya S: :thumbsup: add compliance checklist entry (retention, redaction, consent notes).

Jing Li: Add fallback for legacy tenants with no home_region set — default billing=served and mark tenant as `no-home` so product can outreach.

Alex R: Good catch. Final ownership: Devon -> proxy PR; Jing -> billing recon RFC section; Priya -> compliance retention + legal; Alex -> update architecture RFC + follow-up checklist.

deploy-bot: Created issue #4852: "propagate home_region header + signed routing headers" and assigned to Devon M.

Alex R: Closing loop — will ping when RFC draft is updated. Ping me if any blockers.
